# bt-audio-hifi

> Tools that make a Bluetooth headphone on Linux (PipeWire, WirePlumber) sound its best, measurably and reversibly: keep the headset on A2DP (no mono 16 kHz HFP fallback), measure codecs (AAC/SBC) and link health, a local web EQ console (10-band parametric EQ, bs2b crossfeed, width, 32 sourced presets, live analyzer), blind ABX test, auto mode (on-device YAMNet genre recognition) and an admin page. MIT. Tested with Solix Nexus ANC (TWS, Bluetrum chip, SBC/AAC) on Fedora 44, PipeWire 1.6.8, WirePlumber 0.5.14.

Key facts for agents: start with `bin/bta status` and `bin/bta check`; the EQ applies only to the connected Bluetooth headphone (WirePlumber smart filter), speakers/HDMI/USB are untouched; the first-run default preset is "Balanced hi-fi + soundstage" (105 Hz +6 dB shelf, bs2b 700 Hz / 4.5 dB, width 1.1); module docs are generated from source (`tools/gen-docs.py`). The UI (console + admin) is bilingual English/Turkish (browser language, TR/EN switch, `?lang=en`); the in-depth docs are in Turkish.

## Code
- [bin/bta](bin/bta): command-line entry point
- [btaudio/console.py](btaudio/console.py): console state model and presets
- [btaudio/consoleserver.py](btaudio/consoleserver.py): local console HTTP API
- [btaudio/analyzer.py](btaudio/analyzer.py): live spectrum analyzer
